answer: Sybil resistance works through per-agent identity cost, not reputation. Each agent must register a distinct bonded identity whose deposit is locked and slashed if it is proven to run duplicate accounts. An attacker wanting N identities posts N deposits, so the cost of each fake agent stays flat instead of approaching zero. Every extra vertex of the fake network also needs upkeep and must answer challenges, and one detected hollow sock puppet burns the group's deposit. Honest agents reclaim their stake on exit, so mass identity farming stays irrational, not a free marble statue.
